cues.zh: 看看这个40加仑电热水器上的标签。
cues.en: Take a look at this label on this 40 gallon electric water heater.

cues.zh: 上面列了三个功率：
cues.en: It lists three wattages:

cues.zh: 上部是4500瓦。
cues.en: Upper is 4500W.

cues.zh: 下部也是4500瓦。
cues.en: Lower is also 4500W.

cues.zh: 当然，加起来就是……
cues.en: And of course that totals…
4500 wa - whatt?

cues.zh: 这是谁写的？
cues.en: Who wrote this?

cues.zh: 其实，这不算写错。
cues.en: Actually, that’s not a mistake.

cues.zh: 大多数传统电热水器的标签上都差不多。
cues.en: You’ll find similar labels on most conventional electric water heaters.

cues.zh: 哦对了，顺便说一句，第二个功率是它接208V电源而不是240V时的运行功率，
cues.en: Oh and, by the way, that second listed wattage is what it would run at if hooked up to a 208V electrical supply rather than 240,

cues.zh: 这种电压通常出现在办公室和大型公寓楼里。
cues.en: which you’ll usually find in office and large apartment buildings.

cues.zh: 用欧姆定律可以算出，这个加热元件的电阻是12.8欧姆，
cues.en: Using Ohm’s law we can determine that this thing’s heating element has a resistance of 12.8 ohms,

cues.zh: 在240V下会通过18.75安培电流，也就是4500瓦，
cues.en: which at 240V would draw 18.75 amps and thus 4500 watts

cues.zh: 但在208V下只通过16.25安培，算下来就是3380瓦。
cues.en: but at 208v it would only draw 16.25 amps which works out to 3380W.

cues.zh: 数学真有意思！
cues.en: Math is fun!

cues.zh: 那这两个数字怎么能自己加自己呢？
cues.en: Anyway, how can those two numbers add up to themselves?

cues.zh: 这个标签会让人觉得 2+2 等于 2。
cues.en: This label would suggest 2+2 is 2.

cues.zh: 我很确定那是错的。
cues.en: And I’m pretty confident that’s wrong.

cues.zh: 你可能已经从“上”“下”这两个标签猜到，热水器里有两个独立的加热元件——
cues.en: Well, you might have guessed by the labels “upper” and “lower” that there are two separate heating elements in the water heater -

cues.zh: 确实有，而且它们的额定功率相同。
cues.en: indeed there are, and they’re both the same power rating.

cues.zh: 这个荒唐的算术跟温控器有关。
cues.en: The reason for this silly math has to do with the thermostats.

cues.zh: 没错，温控器也有两个。
cues.en: Yeah, there’s two of those, too.

cues.zh: 但它们巧妙地互锁在一起，不仅防止同时运行导致供电过载，
cues.en: But they’re cleverly interlocked in a way that not only prevents them from running at the same time which would overload the electrical supply

cues.zh: 还让热水器的运行更智能、更高效。
cues.en: but also makes the operation of the water heater smarter and more effective.

cues.zh: 这种热水器是极其简单的设备。
cues.en: A water heater like this is an extremely simple device.

cues.zh: 它其实就是一个保温极好的圆柱形水箱，上面有几个孔。
cues.en: It’s really just an exceptionally well-insulated cylindrical tank of water with a few holes in it.

cues.zh: 顶部有孔，让水进出。
cues.en: Up top there are holes to let water in and out.

cues.zh: 下面还有一个带阀门的孔，让你能定期冲洗水箱，
cues.en: Down below is another hole with a spigot to let you flush out the tank periodically,

cues.zh: 然后水箱两侧这些盖子下面还有两个孔。
cues.en: and then there are two holes in the sides of the tank under these covers.

cues.zh: 加热元件通过这些孔伸进水箱、浸入水中，通电时
cues.en: The heating elements stick into the tank and thus into the water through those holes and when power is run through them

cues.zh: 它们会变得非常烫。
cues.en: they get real hot.

cues.zh: 这其实就是一个超大号的水壶。
cues.en: This is really just an overgrown kettle.

cues.zh: 其实水箱上还有两个孔，其中一个通向顶部的温度/压力安全阀。
cues.en: Now, there are actually two more holes in the tank, one of which leads to the temperature/pressure safety valve up top.

cues.zh: 加热水会让水略微膨胀，从而增加水箱内的压力。
cues.en: Heating water makes it expand slightly which increases the pressure inside the tank.

cues.zh: 通常这不成问题。
cues.en: Ordinarily this isn’t a problem.

cues.zh: 水箱看似是个密封的压力容器，但它仍然与家里其余的水管系统相连。
cues.en: The tank may seem like a sealed pressure vessel but it’s still connected to the rest of your plumbing.

cues.zh: 水箱内的水膨胀时，部分水会通过把供水管里的水往回推而排出水箱。
cues.en: As the water inside expands, some water will simply move out of the tank by pushing the water in the supply line backwards.

cues.zh: 然而，如果你的整套管道系统是完全封闭并带有防回流装置的，
cues.en: However, if you have an entirely closed plumbing system with backflow prevention,

cues.zh: 那就排不出去了，所以你的热水器上多半装有一个膨胀罐。
cues.en: then that won’t be possible so you probably have an expansion tank installed with your water heater.

cues.zh: 至少我希望是这样。
cues.en: At least I hope so.

cues.zh: 但不管怎样，如果因为某种原因，罐内压力开始升得过高，和/或里面的水变得太热，
cues.en: But anyway if for whatever reason pressure starts building up too high in the tank and/or the water inside is getting too hot

cues.zh: 那么这个阀门就会弹开，释放压力，把热水喷到地板上，
cues.en: then this valve will pop open, releasing that pressure and spraying hot water onto the floor,

cues.zh: 那你就惨了，但至少热水器没有爆炸。
cues.en: and you will have a very bad day but at least the water heater didn’t explode.

cues.zh: 这还不错。
cues.en: That’s nice.

cues.zh: 水箱上的最后一个孔是很多人容易忽略的。
cues.en: And the final hole in the tank is one many people overlook.

cues.zh: 因为水箱是钢制的，不知道你听说过没有，钢可不太喜欢长时间接触水，
cues.en: Because the tank is made of steel which, I don’t know if you’ve heard but doesn’t really like to be in prolonged contact with water,

cues.zh: 一根通常由铝或镁制成的牺牲阳极棒会伸入水中，替水箱其余部分承受腐蚀，
cues.en: a sacrificial anode rod often made of aluminum or magnesium pokes down into the water to take the corrosion bullet for the rest of the tank

cues.zh: 防止水箱生锈。
cues.en: and keep it from rusting.

cues.zh: 那根棒的顶端埋在这个插头下面的泡沫隔热层里，
cues.en: The top of that rod lives buried underneath the foam insulation that's underneath this plug,

cues.zh: 而且它其实是可以更换的！
cues.en: and it can actually be replaced!

cues.zh: 如果你定期更换，就能显著延长热水器的寿命。
cues.en: If you do that regularly, it can extend the life of your water heater significantly.

cues.zh: 但几乎没人这么做，包括我自己。
cues.en: But almost nobody does that, including me.

cues.zh: 懒人万岁！
cues.en: Yay laziness!

cues.zh: 不过这不是家居改造频道……
cues.en: But this isn’t a home improvement channel…

cues.zh: 那这台热水器到底有什么特别之处，让我专门为它做一期视频呢？
cues.en: So what's so special about this water heater that’s making me make a video about it?

cues.zh: 刚才我说过，温控器让它更智能、更高效。
cues.en: Well, earlier I said the thermostats make it smarter and more effective.

cues.zh: 让我来解释一下。
cues.en: Allow me to explain.

cues.zh: 注意，虽然这是一台40加仑的热水器，
cues.en: Notice that even though this is a 40 gallon water heater,

cues.zh: 但它的额定容量竟然是53加仑。
cues.en: its rated capacity is somehow 53 gallons.

cues.zh: 那多出来的13加仑是从哪变出来的？
cues.en: Where did it magic 13 extra gallons from?

cues.zh: 我想，我们可以在加热进水的同时把水箱里的水放出来，对吧？
cues.en: Well, I suppose we can let water out of the tank while also heating incoming water, can’t we?

cues.zh: 是的，但还不止这些。
cues.en: Yes, but there’s more to it than just that.

cues.zh: 首先，水究竟是如何流入和流出这个水箱的？
cues.en: First, how exactly does the water flow into and out of this tank?

cues.zh: 两根管道都在顶部，
cues.en: Both pipes are at the top,

cues.zh: 但进水管连接着一根一直延伸到水箱底部的下行管——
cues.en: but the incoming water supply pipe attaches to a dip tube that travels all the way down to the bottom of the tank -

cues.zh: 也就是说，冷水从底部进入水箱，把热水从顶部推出去。
cues.en: meaning cold water enters the tank from below and pushes hot water out the top.

cues.zh: 我们其实可以用热成像仪观察到这一点。
cues.en: We can actually observe this with the thermal camera.

cues.zh: 现在水箱的温度相当均匀，只比环境温度高几度。
cues.en: Right now the tank has a fairly uniform temperature, just a few degrees above ambient.

cues.zh: 但当我打开水龙头开始用热水时，
cues.en: But when I open a tap and start using its hot water,

cues.zh: 我们看到只有水箱底部在变冷。
cues.en: we see that it’s only getting colder at the bottom of the tank.

cues.zh: 而水有一个很有意思的特性：只要减少湍流、让水保持相对静止，
cues.en: And here’s something pretty fascinating about water: so long as you reduce turbulence and keep things relatively still,

cues.zh: 水箱里的热水和冷水就不会混合。
cues.en: the hot and cold water inside the tank doesn’t mix.

cues.zh: 就像这样。
cues.en: Like, at all.

cues.zh: 可以看到，随着我继续使用热水，冷水区域变得越来越大，
cues.en: You can see that as I continue using hot water, the region that’s cold is getting bigger,

cues.zh: 但顶部热水的温度仍然和我刚开始时一样热。
cues.en: but the hot parts up top are still just as hot as they were when I started.

cues.zh: 这是因为热水的密度比冷水小，
cues.en: This happens because hot water is less dense than cold water,

cues.zh: 所以实际上它会“浮”到水箱顶部，结果就在冷热水之间维持了一个出奇清晰的分界线。
cues.en: so in effect it “floats” to the top of the tank, and as a result a surprisingly sharp boundary between hot and cold is maintained.

cues.zh: 你可能会想，随着时间推移，这个分界层会消失，水会混合在一起，但
cues.en: Now you might think that over time that boundary layer will disappear and the water will mix together but

cues.zh: 大多数情况下并不会。
cues.en: for the most part it doesn’t.

cues.zh: 水箱内任何冷却下来的水（比如附着在稍微凉一点的水箱壁上的水）
cues.en: Any water that cools down inside the tank (like for instance the water clinging to the slightly cooler tank walls)

cues.zh: 密度变大，直接沉到底部，和其余冷水堆在一起。
cues.en: becomes more dense and simply sinks to the bottom, piling in with the rest of the cold water.

cues.zh: 很久不给水箱加热后，剩下的热水确实会开始冷却，
cues.en: After a very long time without adding heat energy to the tank the remaining hot water does start to cool down,

cues.zh: 但花的时间比你想象的长得多。
cues.en: but it takes a lot longer than you’d think.

cues.zh: 差不多大半天吧。
cues.en: Like, the better part of a day.

cues.zh: 挺不可思议的。
cues.en: It’s pretty wild.

cues.zh: 这种热分层，加上我们从底部往上注水的方式，
cues.en: This thermal stratification combined with how we fill the tank from the bottom-up

cues.zh: 原来非常有用。
cues.en: turns out to be really useful.

cues.zh: 记住，水箱里有两个不同高度的加热元件。
cues.en: Remember that we have two heating elements sticking into the tank at two different heights.

cues.zh: 随着你不断用热水，冷热水的分界线最终会到达底部加热元件和它的温控器，
cues.en: As you continue using hot water, eventually the cold/hot water boundary reaches the bottom heating element and its thermostat,

cues.zh: 启动那个元件，让它开始加热流入水箱的水。
cues.en: kicking that element on so it can start working to heat the water as it flows into the tank.

cues.zh: 4500瓦听起来功率很大，但在热水加热的语境下，其实真不算什么。
cues.en: Now, 4500 watts may seem like a lot of power, but in the context of water heating it really isn’t.

cues.zh: 加热水需要消耗大量能源。
cues.en: It takes gobs of energy to heat water.

cues.zh: 热水器最多每秒向水中输入4500焦耳，也就是每秒1075.5克卡。
cues.en: At most the water heater can put 4500 joules into the water per second, or 1075.5 gram calories per second.

cues.zh: 在寒冷的冬日，进入水箱的水温如果运气好可能是10摄氏度，
cues.en: On a cold winter day the water entering the tank might be 10 degrees Celsius if we’re lucky,

cues.zh: 而我们的目标温度通常在50摄氏度左右。
cues.en: and our target temperature is generally around 50 degrees Celsius.

cues.zh: 所以我们需要让水温升高40度。
cues.en: So we need to attain a 40 degree temperature rise.

cues.zh: 如果我们把每秒拥有的克卡数除以需要升高的40度，
cues.en: If we divide the gram calories we have every second by the 40 degrees we need to increase in temperature,

cues.zh: 就会发现每秒只能加热26.9毫升水，也就是每分钟约1.6升。
cues.en: we find that we can only heat 26.9 milliliters of water per second, or about 1.6 liters per minute.

cues.zh: 这其实还不算太差，但这里常见的低流量淋浴头最低是每分钟1.5加仑，
cues.en: That’s not too bad, really, but the lowest flow shower heads you’ll generally find here are 1.5 gallons per minute,

cues.zh: 最高可能达到2.5加仑。
cues.en: and they may go as high as 2.5.

cues.zh: 坚持用较小的数字，那大约是每分钟5.7升的流量。
cues.en: Sticking with the smaller number, that’s nearly 5.7 liters per minute of flow.

cues.zh: 当然，大多数人会用一点冷水来调温热水
cues.en: Of course most people temper hot water with a bit of cold water

cues.zh: 所以每分钟可能只有4升水离开热水箱
cues.en: so we might only have 4 liters leaving the hot water tank every minute

cues.zh: 但这仍然是我们用4500瓦所能加热的水量的两倍多。
cues.en: but that’s still more than double what we can heat with 4500 watts.

cues.zh: 所以我们最终会用完热水。
cues.en: So we’re going to run out of hot water eventually.

cues.zh: 这实在是无法避免的。
cues.en: There’s just no getting around that.

cues.zh: 即使我们尝试在水进入水箱时加热它，
cues.en: Even if we try and heat the water as it enters the tank,

cues.zh: 水的流出速度实在太快，等我们用完水箱里已有的热水时，它根本达不到目标温度。
cues.en: the water is simply moving out too quickly and it won’t reach the target temperature by the time we’ve used up the hot water already in it.

cues.zh: 但是，记住底部加热元件上方还有第二个加热元件。
cues.en: But, remember there’s a second heating element above the one at the bottom.

cues.zh: 它并不更强大
cues.en: It isn’t any more powerful

cues.zh: 但稍加策略，我们就能用它来追赶离开水箱的水。
cues.en: but with a bit of strategy we can use it to chase the water as it leaves the tank.

cues.zh: 而这正是热水器的工作原理。
cues.en: And that’s exactly what the water heater does.

cues.zh: 按照我们理论上的每分钟4升流速，底部加热元件只能实现约16度的温升。
cues.en: With our theoretical 4 liters per minute flow rate, the lower heating element will only achieve about a 16 degree temperature rise.

cues.zh: 这远远不够，但也不是毫无作用。
cues.en: That's nowhere enough, but also that’s not nothing.

cues.zh: 只要底部元件处于开启状态，
cues.en: So long as the lower element is turned on,

cues.zh: 实际上水箱底部注入的就是26度的水
cues.en: in effect the bottom of the tank is filling up with 26 degree water

cues.zh: 而不是10度的水。
cues.en: rather than 10 degree water.

cues.zh: 一旦这些温水到达顶部元件，
cues.en: And once that tepid water reaches the top element,

cues.zh: 这时它的恒温器启动，把功率输出切换给自己。
cues.en: well now its thermostat kicks in and switches the power output to itself.

cues.zh: 我们仍然是同样的4500瓦，但现在是在这里——
cues.en: We have the same 4500 watts that we did before, but now it’s up here -

cues.zh: 用来加热我们已经开始加热的水。
cues.en: working to heat the water we’ve already started heating.

cues.zh: 在每分钟4升的流速下，我们仍然只能实现16度的温升，
cues.en: We can still only achieve a 16 degree temperature rise with 4 liters per minute of flow,

cues.zh: 但这能把水温提升到42度。
cues.en: but that’ll get us up to 42 degrees.

cues.zh: 还没到理想状态，但也够热了。
cues.en: Not exactly where we want to be, but still plenty hot.

cues.zh: 当然，热水还是会用完——顶部元件一启动，底部就关闭了，
cues.en: We will of course still run out of hot water - once the top element kicks on the bottom switches off,

cues.zh: 所以进水箱的水现在是真的冷，一旦它升到接近顶部……
cues.en: so the water entering the tank is now truly cold and once it’s up near the top...

cues.zh: 那就完了。
cues.en: well, game over.

cues.zh: 现在水箱里最多只能出26度的水。
cues.en: At best we’re getting 26 degree water out of the tank, now.

cues.zh: 但这个策略让我们在有限电源下多争取了一些时间，仅仅是通过改变供电位置，把同样的水加热了两次。
cues.en: But this strategy bought us some extra time with a limited power source simply by changing where we applied that power, and heating the same water twice.

cues.zh: 这就是我们凭空多出13加仑热水的原因。
cues.en: This is where we magicked 13 extra gallons from.

cues.zh: 4500瓦就是每秒4500焦耳，也就是每小时1620万焦耳，即387万克卡路里。
cues.en: 4500 watts is 4500 joules per second, and that's 16.2 million joules per hour or 3.87 million gram calories.

cues.zh: 能把96.8升水升高40摄氏度。
cues.en: And lift 96.8 liters of water by 40 degrees celsius.

cues.zh: 所以一小时内，这个热水器能把25.5加仑冷水加热到目标温度，
cues.en: So over an hour, this water heater can bring 25.5 gallons of cold water to our target temperature,

cues.zh: 这就是“第一小时额定值”的由来。
cues.en: and that is where this “1st hour rating” comes from.

cues.zh: 我估计标称的13加仑其实超过了真实容量
cues.en: I reckon it’s only listed as 13 gallons over the true capacity

cues.zh: 因为这是按208V供电算的，还假设一开始是冰冷的水。
cues.en: since it was calculated using a 208V supply and assuming we start with freezing cold water.

cues.zh: 相当保守。
cues.en: Quite conservative.

cues.zh: 总之，这意味着在一小时内，它能给冷水加入的能量，加上它储存在40加仑热水中的能量
cues.en: In any case, this means that over an hour the energy it can add to cold water plus the energy it has stored in 40 gallons of already hot water

cues.zh: 等同于一开始就有53加仑。
cues.en: is the same as if you had 53 gallons in the first place.

cues.zh: 而在240V电压下，就像我这里这样，可能接近65加仑。
cues.en: And on 240V like I have here it may be closer to, like 65 gallons.

cues.zh: 这里采用的策略简直是天才，尤其考虑到这个设备如此简单。
cues.en: The strategy employed here is frankly genius, especially considering how simple this device is.

cues.zh: 我们只有两个最普通的恒温器。
cues.en: All we have are two bog-standard thermostats.

cues.zh: 这里没有电子元件，没有控制方案，每个加热元件就配一个恒温器。
cues.en: There are no electronics here, there’s no control scheme, it’s just a thermostat for each heating element.

cues.zh: 电路设计唯一的复杂之处在于顶部恒温器始终优先。
cues.en: The only complication to the circuit design is that the top thermostat always takes priority.

cues.zh: 如果那个加热元件开启，恒温器就会断开下方元件的电路，防止它运行。
cues.en: If that heating element is switched on, the thermostat breaks the circuit to the lower element to prevent it from running.

cues.zh: 现在，你可能会觉得这会造成某种运行冲突。
cues.en: Now, you might think this would cause some sort of operational conflict.

cues.zh: 如果我们想让底部恒温器运行，但顶部恒温器恰好启动了，该怎么办？
cues.en: What if we want the bottom thermostat to run but the top one happens to have kicked on?

cues.zh: 嗯，想一下这个：
cues.en: Well, think about this for a sec:

cues.zh: 因为热水自然会留在水箱顶部，而我们注入的冷水从底部进入，
cues.en: because hot water stays at the top of the tank naturally, and we fill it with cold water comes in at the bottom,

cues.zh: 大多数情况下这种情况不会发生。
cues.en: for the most part that just doesn't happen.

cues.zh: 事实上，顶部元件几乎根本用不上。
cues.en: In fact, top element rarely gets used at all.

cues.zh: 它基本上只在你用掉水箱中一半以上的水之后才会启动。
cues.en: It basically only comes on after you have used up more than half of the water in the tank.

cues.zh: 如果你用的水没那么多，底部元件就会处理。
cues.en: If you don’t use at least that much, the bottom element will take care of things.

cues.zh: 在两次使用之间保持水箱温暖也是同样的道理。
cues.en: Same goes for keeping the tank warm between uses.

cues.zh: 用低流量花洒的话，淋浴15分钟用水量不太可能超过20加仑。
cues.en: And with a low-flow shower head, 15 minutes in the shower is unlikely to use much more than 20 gallons of water.

cues.zh: 所以，上面那个元件根本不需要运行。
cues.en: So, yeah, the top one just doesn't need to run.

cues.zh: 但如果你真的把热水全用光了，或者哪怕只是快用光了，
cues.en: But if you do happen to use up all the hot water, or even just come close to that,

cues.zh: 那么给顶部元件优先级的策略就又能帮上忙了。
cues.en: well now the strategy of giving the top element priority helps us again.

cues.zh: 当然，我们可以只用底部元件来加热水，
cues.en: While we can of course use the bottom element alone to heat the water,

cues.zh: 毕竟它在底部产生的热水会浮到顶部，
cues.en: after all the hot water it generates down there will float up to the top,

cues.zh: 但那样做意味着我们得一次性加热整箱水。
cues.en: doing that means we have to heat the entire volume in one go.

cues.zh: 它在底部产生的热水在上升途中必须穿过所有冷水，这当然会让热水冷却下来。
cues.en: Whatever hot water it generates at the bottom has to travel through all the cold water on its way up to the top which will of course cool it down.

cues.zh: 哦，顺便提一下，每当元件在主动加热时，
cues.en: Oh, by the way, I should mention that whenever the elements are actively heating,

cues.zh: 水箱内的水会因为产生的对流而出现一些混合和翻搅。
cues.en: there is some mixing and churning of the water going on inside the tank thanks to the convection currents that generates.

cues.zh: 你可以看到这个水壶里发生的情况。
cues.en: You can see that happening here with this kettle.

cues.zh: 这就是我们如何用相当于两根热棒的东西加热整箱水。
cues.en: That’s how we can heat the entire tank of water using what amounts to two hot sticks.

cues.zh: 总之，如果我们想把40加仑冷水加热40摄氏度，
cues.en: Anyway, if we want to heat 40 gallons of cold water by 40 degrees celsius,

cues.zh: 那将需要超过600万卡路里，也就是大约7039瓦时。
cues.en: it’s gonna take over 6 million calories or about 7039 watt-hours.

cues.zh: 有4500瓦可用功率，那大约需要一个半小时。
cues.en: With 4500 watts to play with, that’s gonna take about an hour and a half.

cues.zh: 然而，如果我们只给顶部加热元件供电，那么实际上我们只需要加热一半的水。
cues.en: However, if we only send power to the top element, then in effect we only have to heat half of the water.

cues.zh: 我们仍然会在加热元件周围产生一些对流，但不会把所有的水混合在一起——
cues.en: We’ll still get some convection currents around the element, but we won’t be mixing all of the water together -

cues.zh: 水箱底部会保持冷水。
cues.en: the bottom of the tank will stay cold.

cues.zh: 因此，我们能让水箱顶部的水（记住，这些水会最先流出）在一半时间内达到我们想要的温度。
cues.en: So we’ll get the water in the top of the tank (which remember is what leaves first) up to our desired temperature in half the time.

cues.zh: 所以即使热水完全用光了，也只要大约45分钟，你就能再次得到真正滚烫的热水。
cues.en: So even after completely running out of hot water, you’ll get truly hot water again after only 45 minutes or so.

cues.zh: 只有等那部分水变暖并“就绪”后，我们才会把电力重新送到底部加热元件，去加热剩下的水。
cues.en: Only once that’s warm and “ready” will we send power back down to the bottom element to heat up the rest.

cues.zh: 我知道我有点怪，但我觉得这太神奇了！
cues.en: I know that I’m weird, but I think this is amazing!

cues.en: I only recently learned that there are two thermostats on the water heater.

cues.zh: 事后想想，这本来应该更明显一点，毕竟，你知道的，前面有两个一模一样的盖子，但
cues.en: In hindsight it probably should have been a little more obvious since, y’know, there’s two identical covers on the front but

cues.zh: 我当时只是以为那是为了省成本之类的，还以为只有一个温控器同时控制两个加热元件。
cues.en: I just assumed that was for cost cutting or something and thought there was one thermostat controlling both elements.

cues.zh: 好吧，严格来说现在也还是这样，但……你懂我意思。
cues.en: Well, OK I guess there still is, technically, but… y’know what I mean.

cues.zh: 热水在水箱里如何流动的简单物理原理，让我们得以实现一种非常有策略的加热方式
cues.en: The simple physics of how hot water behaves in a tank allowed us to implement a very strategic method of heating it

cues.zh: 只靠一根浸入管和两个联锁的温控器就够了。
cues.en: using nothing but a dip tube and two interlocked thermostats.

cues.zh: 做到这些，基本就涵盖了所有可能的问题：
cues.en: Just doing that covers pretty much all possible concerns:

cues.zh: 如何以最快速度加热冷水箱获得热水，如何在出水过程中追加热量以增加储备容量，
cues.en: how best to heat a cold tank for the fastest-possible hot water, how to chase it on its way out for some extra reserve capacity,

cues.zh: 以及如何用更合理的输入功率同时实现这两点。
cues.en: and how to do both those things with a more reasonable amount of input power.

cues.zh: 这就是我所说的……妙！
cues.en: And that’s what I call … neat!

cues.en: You might have noticed that the water heater is hooked up to some sort of mystery box.

cues.en: See, I’m in the middle of some experiments.

cues.zh: 正如我说的，热水器的保温性能极好。
cues.en: Water heaters, as I said, are exceptionally well insulated.

cues.zh: 实际上，你摸水箱会觉得冰凉，根本想不到里面有40加仑滚烫的热水。
cues.en: In fact you would have no idea there’s 40 gallons of piping hot water in there by touching the tank as it feels stone cold.

cues.zh: 你能真正感觉到的热量，只有从供水管漏出来的那点——我真该给那些管子包上保温套。
cues.en: The only heat you can really feel is what leaks out of the supply pipes - I really oughta get some sleeves for those.

cues.zh: 总之，因为这东西保温太好，所以它实际上就是一块电池。
cues.en: Anyway, because this thing is so well-insulated that means it’s effectively a battery.

cues.zh: 还记得我之前算的那笔账吗？
cues.en: Remember that math I did earlier?

cues.en: It takes over 7 kilowatt-hours to heat up 40 gallons of water by 40 degrees C.

cues.en: And that’s… a lot!

cues.en: Electric water heaters are among the most power-hungry things in your life,

cues.zh: 而运行它们的成本，是很多人改用燃气烧热水的一大原因。
cues.en: and the cost to operate them is a big reason many people chose to use gas instead for water heating.

cues.en: Now, I have a time-of-use rate plan with my utility and power in the middle of the night is quite cheap.

cues.zh: 所以在过去几个月里，我只让这玩意儿在凌晨1点到5点之间运行。
cues.en: So for the past couple of months, I have only been letting this thing operate between 1 and 5 AM.

cues.en: But in fairness, that could be a risk and more research is definitely needed there,

cues.en: so I am not endorsing this practice. Do not do this at home.

cues.zh: 不过我可以告诉你，当那个东西“充满能量”之后
cues.en: I can however tell you that when that thing is “charged up”

cues.zh: 它的保温时间会比我以为的极限长得多得多得多。
cues.en: it will stay hot for way way wayyy longer than I thought was remotely possible.

cues.zh: 我晚上9点洗过澡——也就是说热水器已经16个小时没工作了！——水还是烫得吓人。
cues.en: I've taken a shower at 9:00 at night - meaning the water heater had not operated for sixteen hours! - and the water was still scaldingly hot.

cues.en: Five hours later - five hours of the water heater being entirely off -

cues.en: the water measured 124.3 degrees.

cues.zh: 就是把数字调换了一下。
cues.en: Just swapped the digits around.

cues.en: Somehow, even with at least 10 gallons of cold water sitting in the bottom of the tank for five hours,

cues.en: It’s wild but the cold and hot water really just don’t mix.

cues.en: But I think it’s worth pointing out that this thing hardly loses any energy when it’s not getting used.

cues.zh: 这使它成为一个非常有效的储能设备——而且还是个大型的！
cues.en: And that makes it a really effective energy storage device - and a large one at that!

cues.en: But I can already say with complete confidence that a conventional, tanked water heater can be an important part of an energy-management strategy.
